notes.title: Update 4 OUT NOW and VR Launch Update!
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders!



The fourth post-launch update which comes with a huge list of improvements, balancing and fixes is out now. These include a special focus on post-game content: "Threat Levels" and a re-work of the Overclock system.



We have an update regarding the VR version coming to Steam. Due to an unexpected technical issue with the game, the launch of the VR version has been delayed to next week. We apologise for this inconvenience and want to ensure that you have the best possible experience when playing. We promise to keep you updated on the situation and to let you know once the VR version is officially out next week.



Thank you so much for understanding and for always supporting our game, in the mean time, we hope you enjoy the changes in update 4. We'd love to hear what you think, so let us know by joining our Discord server and sharing your feedback.


Threat Level Rising


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/889b4d26d98cfacd32a00ef871647a05b4606a96.jpg"]

Threat Levels have been activated across all regions, marking the beginning of a new post-game campaign. Each region now comes with five escalating Threat Levels. The further you push, the tougher enemies become.


Every Threat Level comes with a set of Directives, high-risk challenges that must be completed in a single mission. Succeeding earns you Medals, Command’s new currency for unlocking higher Threat Levels.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/987381d2077754e3885f131d30e02a68aaa6af07.jpg"]

Combat balance has been overhauled to match the rising challenge, so expect tougher fights, tighter margins, and deadlier choices. The War Room’s been retooled to support this new structure. You’ll find Threat Levels front and centre in mission prep, making it easier to track your progress and plan your next deployment.  



To read more about Threat Levels, check out our preview post from last week.


Overclocks Reforged


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/d216011ea36869f4876aee63893a74b9e9c897f7.jpg"]

We also recently posted a preview of the Overclocks re-work! You can find it here in case you missed it.



Overclocks are no longer tucked away in the Mech Yard, but now earned in the thick of battle. You’ll unlock and equip them mid-run, shaping your firepower and tactics in real time. If you spent Intelligence or Blueprints unlocking Advancements or Overclocks before, Command’s issuing full refunds.


Overclocks are now organised into 10 specialist categories, each one pushing your mechs in a new tactical direction. Not every mech can access every category, so you’ll need to know your unit and make your choices count.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/77d295cf6e2695ed4da41bb133d7d5015f3b5687.jpg"]

Power (the way Overclocks are unlocked) has also changed. It’s now fuelled directly by Boosts and Enhancements: each one you slot in adds to your Overclock ‘Power’ capacity. We’ve lowered the thresholds to get you into the action faster, and you’ll see your Power Level front and centre when selecting upgrades. 



We also added a new Overclock reward screen and upgraded the Squad Overview so you can track your build at a glance.


Command is also dropping 43 brand-new Overclocks into the rotation. Some existing ones have been reworked, others reassigned as Enhancements, and one decommissioned entirely. 


ChangelistThreat Levels
Added Threat Levels which scale the difficulty of the region.

Added Directives which reward Medals to unlock Threat Levels.

Added 'View Directives' button to Region Map to track progress.

End of Run Module rewards quality is now determined by Threat Level instead of Region.

End of Run rewards now show what Directives were completed on that run.

Run History now shows what Threat Level it was played on.

Runs from before this update will display as 'Threat Level 1'

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/cb47efa0a919e997a1efa4fcec809e2c7e4f5414.jpg"]
Overclocks
Overclocks have been changed from a meta reward to a run reward.

The Mechanical Surge Advancement and any Overclocks unlocked before this update will have the Intelligence and Blueprints refunded.

Overclocks are now categorised into 10 specialisations with only certain mechs having access to each Overclock specialisation.

Power for Overclocks is now granted by Boosts and Enhancements, each one equipped giving 1 Power.

Power required for Overclocks reduced from 4, 12, 20 to 4, 8, 12.

Mech Power Level is now shown when selecting a Boost or Enhancement.

Added a new reward screen for when you are choosing an Overclock.

Improved Overclocks visuals on the Squad Overview.

Overclocks are now displayed in the Run History.

Adjusted pre-existing Overclocks:

Apex Hunter renamed to Apex Sniper.

Deadeye renamed to Sniper.

Flawless Fury renamed Flawless Sentinel and now increases Repair instead of Damage.

Last Siphon renamed to Redline and Health Threshold reduced from <50% to <40%.

Phoenix Protocol renamed to Redline Protocol and can now trigger once every combat instead of once every mission but only restores 10% health, down from 50%.

First Strike has been renamed to Lethal Overwatch.

Ward of Steel has been renamed to Aegis Ward.

Changed Vigor Rage to a Forge Industries Enhancement.

Changed Shell Striker to a Warhead Enhancement.

Removed Gold-Tipped Rounds.



Added 43 new Overclocks:

Aegis - While this mech is stationary, it gains Barrier every 5 seconds.

Reactive Aegis - When this mech is attacked, a nearby ally gains a stack of Barrier.

Aegis Echo - When this mech gains Barrier, a nearby ally also gains a stack of Barrier.

Aegis Conduit - When this mech loses a stack of Barrier, a nearby ally has some health restored.

Bastion - At the start of each wave, this mech gains armour.

Bastion Cascade - When this mech gains armour, a nearby ally gains a percentage of the armour also.

Bastion Reserves - When this mech restores health in combat, it gains a percentage of the health as armour.

Enduring Bastion - At the end of each wave, if this mech took damage, its repair is increased for the rest of the mission.

Spiked Bastion - While Armoured, when this mech is attacked, it reflects damage back at the attacker.

Deadlock - Each time this mech attacks it gains fire rate, stacking up to 10 times. This bonus is lost when this mech stops attacking.

Deadlock Breach - Every 5th attack this mech makes against a Weak enemy deals massively increased damage.

Deadlock Calibration - Every 5th attack this mech makes against an enemy mech increases its damage for the rest of the mission.

Deadlock Echo - Every 5th attack this mech makes against the same target will cause a Double Tap.

Deadlock Harvest - Every 5th attack this mech makes against an Armoured enemy, it gains armour.

Executioner - This mech's attacks deal increased damage to enemies at low health.

Executioner's Edge - Every 5th enemy this mech kills increases its critical chance for the rest of the mission.

Executioner's Feast - When this mech kills an enemy with a critical hit, it restores health.

Executioner's Streak - Every enemy this mech kills increases its damage and critical hit damage. These bonuses are lost upon taking damage.

Executioner's Wrath - Every 5th enemy this mech kills increases its damage for the rest of the mission.

Overwatch - When this mech has been stationary for 5 seconds its attack range is increased.

Enduring Overwatch - When this mech remains stationary for an entire wave, its maximum health is increased for the rest of the mission.

Deadly Overwatch - Each time this mech kills an enemy its damage is increased. This bonus is lost when this mech moves.

Critical Overwatch - While this mech is stationary, it gains critical hit chance every 5 seconds.

Phalanx - When this mech has allies nearby, they all gain increased damage resistance.

Phalanx Barrage - When this mech has allies nearby, they all gain increased fire rate.

Phalanx Guardian - When this mech is destroyed, a nearby ally gains increased health and repair for the rest of the mission.

Phalanx Reprisal - When this mech is attacked, a nearby allies next attack deals increased damage.

Phalanx Resolve - When this mech kills an enemy, a nearby ally restores health.

Adrenal Redline - While at low health, this mech's fire rate and movement speed are increased every second, stacking up to 100 times.

Tempering Redline - While at low health, this mech has increased damage resistance.

Vengeful Redline - While at low health, each time this mech takes damage, its damage is increased for the rest of the mission.

Sentinel - At the end of each wave, if this mech is at high health, its gains armour.

Enduring Sentinel - At the end of each combat, if this Mech is at high health, its health is increased for the rest of the mission.

Iron Sentinel - Every 10 seconds this mech doesn't take damage, it gains armour.

Resilient Sentinel - While this mech is at high health, its damage resistance is increased.

Disciplined Sniper - Every third attack this mech makes against Distant enemies deals increased damage.

Elevated Sniper - While this mech is on High Ground, it has increased critical hit chance and critical hit damage.

Relentless Sniper - When this mech critically hits a Distant enemy, its critical chance is increased for the rest of the mission.

Stalker - While this mech is Alone, its critical chance and critical damage is increased.

Stalker's Ambush - Every 5 seconds this mech spends Alone, it gains increased fire rate, stacking up to 10 times. This bonus is lost when this mech moves.

Stalker's Reach - While this mech is Alone, its attack range is increased.

Stalker's Resurgence - When this mech kills an enemy while Alone, it restores health.

Stalker's Stabilizer - At the end of each wave, if this mech is Alone, its repair is increased for the rest of the mission.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/b944d96fd5797536b841670f2d4f4dfc49600654.jpg"]
General Improvements
Cover can now be taken advantage of from either side.

We have also disabled Cover tile indicators as they felt unnecessary now that Cover is 2-sided.

Cover throughout every level in every region has been rearranged to work better with the new 2-sided system.

Extract Objectives now move independently but there speed has been reduced.

Extract Objectives now show the path they will take.

Wave Start/End effects now trigger during Boss Fights.

Enhancement Upgrades now only appear as rewards once you have at least 3 Enhancements.

Repair Kit wont start appearing until a unit is below 80% health, down from 90%.

End of Run Module rewards are now given after your first ever run.

Command Centre Research Tasks can now be progressed on the first run.


Gameplay Balance
All Regions difficulty has been re-balanced. The difficulty curve is now a lot smoother between Regions/Threat Levels than previously where each Region had a big difficulty jump.

Increased Hidden Node count in New Germany from 6 to 8

Western Europe Boss now fires its Mortar Cannon less frequently.

Enemy waves in the Western Europe Boss now spawn less frequently and ramp up in difficulty slower.

Enemy waves in the Scandinavia Boss now spawn less frequently.

Enemy waves in the British Isles Boss now spawn more frequently and start off harder.

All Scandinavian Levels have had adjustments to make them easier to navigate.

Many levels across all Regions have been adjusted to improve gameplay.

Increased Movement Speed of Enemy Heavy Tanks.

Increased Movement Speed of all Player Units

Command Vehicle Movement Speed increased from 10 to 15.

Thunderhead Movement Speed increased from 10 to 15.

Draqan Movement Speed increased from 20 to 25.

Ironclad Movement Speed increased from 15 to 20.

Vulcano Movement Speed increased from 10 to 15.

Steelhawk Movement Speed increased from 20 to 25.

Leadslug Movement Speed increased from 15 to 20.

Warbringer Movement Speed increased from 15 to 20.

Clusterstorm Movement Speed increased from 20 to 25.

Meltdown Movement Speed increased from 20 to 25.

Increased effectiveness of Field Repair Ability Upgrades.

Increased effectiveness of Field Sentry Ability Upgrades.

Field Sentry upgrades now increases its health instead of its critical chance.

Increased Field Sentry's attack range from 2 to 3.

Increased Field Sentry's critical chance from 10% to 25%.

Increased damage gained from Forge Armour's damage upgrade.

Increased ability charges gained from Mine Drops ability charge upgrade.

Increased ability charges gained from Airstrikes ability charge upgrade.

Increased ability charges gained from Jump Jets ability charge upgrade.

Increased ability charges gained from Airstrike ability charge upgrade.

Mechano-Arm now starts with 4 ability charges, down from 6.

Forge Armour now starts with 4 ability charges, down from 5.

Increased cooldown of Mechano-Arm from 20 to 25 but also increased cooldown reduction gained from its cooldown upgrade.

Ability Charges no longer appear as a mid-level reward.

Ability Recharger item at the Scavenger now restores 2 ability charges and now has a much higher possibility of restoring 3.

Enduring Regens health gain has been reduced from 10/20/35/50/75 to 5/10/15/20/30.

Savage Fortitudes health gain has been reduced from 20/30/40/50/75 to 10/20/30/40/50.

Vengeful Resurge healing has been reduced from 50/75/100/150/200 to 30/60/90/120/150.

Weakpoint Recharge ability charge chance reduced from 5/10/15/20/25% to 2/4/6/8/10%.

Volatile Defense has had its internal cooldown on the Disable proc increased and on the Armour proc decreased.


Settings
Removed the "Graphics Quality" setting which previously affected shadows, lighting, texture resolution and anti-aliasing.

Added a Shadow Quality setting which defaults to High.

Added a Texture Quality setting which defaults to High.

Added an Anti-Aliasing setting which defaults to 4x (previously 8x, which is still an option).

Added an Ambient Occlusion setting which defaults to On.


Optimisations
Optimised level geometry to reduce overlapping and unnecessary polygons.

Reworked attack VFX for the Warbringer to improve performance, especially when multiple Warbringers are active at once.

Added a throttling system to prevent too many VFX piling up on a single tile at once.

Reworked level backgrounds to reduce complexity and rendering cost.

Reworked tile indicator logic to improve CPU performance and reduce rendering cost, especially when a unit is selected.


Bug Fixes
Fixed Mechano-Arm Critical Plating Augment increasing Armour instead of Health.

Fixed Combat Text sometimes appearing as though its a critical hit even though it isn't a critical.

Fixed Repair Kit reward choices displaying mech image twice instead of the reward icon.

Fixed health bar colours being inconsistent on the gameplay hud and squad overview.

Fixed being able to assign Pilot Abilities to the Command Vehicle during the squad setup.

Fixed Enemy Units continuing to shoot at Extract Vehicle after the Objective is completed.



...and that wraps up the changes from Update 4! As mentioned at the top of this post, your support and feedback mean everything to us. We'd love to hear from you, so consider joining the Megabit Discord server to talk us directly about the new update and any queries you have regarding the VR news.

See you on the battlefield!



The Grit and Valor - 1949

notes.title: Post-Launch Update 2: Chain of Command
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders!

With this update, our goal is to put tactical command firmly in your hands. We're introducing new tools to coordinate your squad with greater precision, whether it’s by locking onto high-value targets, setting unit-specific priorities, or issuing instant regroup orders in the heat of battle. 

Every change is designed to deepen your strategic options and reward smart decision-making on the field.

Tactical Improvements

New Command: Regroup

When things get messy, you need to pull back fast and smart. That’s where Regroup comes in. One command, and every unit in your squad will rally to a point you choose. No fumbling, no delay. You can issue it with a quick click of the Regroup button at the bottom right of your HUD, or by using your assigned keyboard or gamepad binding. Use it wisely, it might just save your squad.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/edaafae6c0157e2ee85ca371c01149c4760cc8d4.gif
New System: Target Priorities

Outnumbered? Surrounded? Doesn’t matter, what matters is who you hit first. With the new Target Priorities system, each of your mechs follow orders the way you see fit. You set the rules, they execute. Choose from the following priorities:

 Type
 Weak
 Healthy
 Injured
 Far
 Close
 Access this feature through the Squad Overview by clicking the button on your HUD, or use your assigned keyboard or gamepad binding. Once you’re in, you’ll see toggles on each unit to set their priorities.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/7ee3095b1750b04fadb114c3d5217e4bb7bf994f.gif
New Option: Focus Fire

Sometimes it’s not about who's the biggest threat, it’s about finishing the job. With Focus Fire, your units will stay locked on their target until it’s scrap, no matter what else steps into range. You can toggle this setting for each unit in the Squad Overview.

New Command: Mark Target
With this new command, you can manually designate a priority target on the battlefield using your mouse or gamepad cursor. Once marked, that enemy will be focused down by your squad, ignoring all other orders.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/b40d4ce53c7c4051c901fcb4edb993cb71306aad.gif
Thank You, Commander 
Before we get into the rest of the update changes below, we wanted to say a thank you for your continued support. To celebrate the latest update, we’re giving all players a new Command Vehicle skin which you'll be automatically granted upon downloading the update. This is our way of showing appreciation for being part of the Resistance. Equip your new looks, hit the battlefield, and show your enemies what style under pressure really looks like!

notes.title: Dev Diary #2: Cover Deep Dive
notes.content:
Hey everyone – Kevin here again with another Dev Diary! This time, we’re diving deeper into one of the core gameplay mechanics: Cover.

Since launch, we’ve gotten a lot of feedback about how cover works in the game – especially around our decision to make it 1-sided (offers protection in only one direction) instead of 2-sided (protection from both directions).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/bc59c5ddbdf7238dd7f7e1f8581decc71f6b3b98.png

To be honest, most of the feedback has leaned critical, or at least confused. Outside of our dev team, not many players have spoken in favor of 1-sided cover – and even within the team, there are folks who’d prefer the 2-sided approach.

These kinds of design choices are always tricky during development, so I wanted to share a bit of insight into how we made the call, and what the pros and cons of each setup look like.

1-sided Cover
Pros:

 Encourages more strategic positioning – players need to be mindful of where enemies are coming from.
 Promotes level exploration, as players move around to find cover that works based on the direction of threat.
 Gives players a tactical advantage – enemies are much less likely to benefit from cover.
 Cons:
 Doesn’t always make sense visually – why would a wall only protect from one side?
 Can be frustrating when a seemingly good piece of cover becomes useless just because enemies show up from the "wrong" direction.

2-sided Cover
Pros:

 Feels more intuitive and realistic – a wall should offer protection on both sides.
 Makes cover more universally useful, which could help reinforce it as a core mechanic instead of something players forget about.
 It adds to the tactical challenge – if enemies use cover against you, that’s on your positioning. You either take the cover yourself or deny it to the enemy by repositioning.

Cons:

 Players might end up dancing around a single block of cover depending on enemy spawns, rather than moving around the map. (see diagram below).
 If cover takes damage from both sides, it could get destroyed really quickly. That might balance things out and make players move around the map more, but could also make cover feel weak or temporary.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/44721ffad3fdabcc72c03dd00423b6e418a0bbcb.png
We have started to prototype 2-sided cover and discovered a couple of bugs so far but generally the bulk of the work would come from going into each level and making sure:
[olist]
 Cover isn’t  too advantageous if it suddenly became 2-sided, and possibly therefore stripping some cover out or moving it around.
 Cover isn’t too weak now it takes damage from both sides and needs a further balance pass on each level (or again some rearrangement).
[/olist]
As you can probably tell, we’re still torn on which direction to go. We’d love to hear your thoughts to help us decide!

In the meantime, we’ll keep testing and share more updates in the next Dev Diary.

Thanks for reading everyone – and enjoy your weekend!
Kevin

notes.title: Dev Diary #1: Post-Launch Reflections
notes.content:
Hi everyone, Kevin here — Producer on the project.

It’s now been around six weeks since the game launched, and we’ve had some time to reflect on the release, the state of the game, and all the feedback we've received. I wanted to take a moment to share some of those reflections with you and give a clearer picture of where we’re heading.

Launch and First Impressions
Game launches are never easy. You spend years building something, then release it into the world and hope that players connect with it as deeply as you do. It’s an emotional moment — a mix of relief, joy, and (let’s be honest) a bit of fear, and a lot of hitting "refresh" on Steam reviews!
That said, we’re really proud of the game we released. The launch went smoothly overall, and while reviews have ranged from okay to good, we’re taking everything on board. A 77% review score in the strategy genre isn’t bad — especially given how savvy and discerning this audience is. The general consensus seems to be: “There’s a solid foundation here, but room for improvement.” We agree.

Top Themes in Player Feedback
Here's a quick summary of the key feedback we've seen so far:


 Core gameplay is fun but lacks tactical depth
 Core gameplay is fun but lacks variety (e.g., things you experience in runs and ability to change things up mid-run)
 The roguelite grind can feel frustrating
 Game balance needs further refinement
 Certain gameplay elements feel frustrating (notably: Hazards, repetitive VO, and the Cover system)
 Some players expected a turn-based experience similar to Into the Breach


There’s a lot to unpack here. We're a small team, so we’re taking things step by step — prioritising, testing, and listening. While I can’t promise every piece of feedback will be addressed immediately, I can promise to keep sharing what we’re working on and to keep the conversation going.

What We're Working on Right Now
Here’s what we’re currently focused on (and I’ll dive into these more in future posts — some of them deserve their own breakdown):

Cover - 1-sided vs. 2-sided
There’s been plenty of feedback to say that cover should be two-sided, one-sided cover doesn’t make sense etc. and we understand where people are coming from. Cover has always been one-sided to make it a clear tactical advantage to the player rather than something that enemies will also benefit from....but given the weight of feedback, two-sided cover is something we’re testing out.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/e98027c64010b48f74600dc23b7282d4cee4556d.gif

Re-group Command & Enemy Prioritisation
Players have been asking for more tactical control and less micro-management — a tricky balance, but one we’re working toward. To help with that, we’ve been testing a new regroup command, along with a feature that lets you set priority levels for your units. Both of these should cut down on the need for constant individual clicks and repositioning, while still giving you room to plan more strategically — without slowing things down for players who prefer a more fast-paced, action-heavy style.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/95ad85828193e497b3f56d2496905d714d037232.gif

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/5764ba85225e64d643b60edb8e1152a7832caa61.gif

Surfacing more useful information
Players have been asking for clearer, more detailed info to help make better choices around upgrades and progression. We’re updating menus and tooltips to show more stats — including comparisons where it makes sense. So far, we’ve focused on areas like the Pilot Barracks and Ability stats, Mechyard tooltips, and the run overview. We’ll keep refining and expanding as we go.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/602dff698a5d29165312506991ae65fc71ed6931.png

That’s it for now — just a quick update to let you know where our heads are at. Massive thanks to everyone who’s played the game, shared feedback, or just taken the time to care. It really does mean a lot.

Thanks everyone,
Kevin

notes.title: Patch Notes: Display Settings and Other Fixes
notes.content:
Greeting, Commanders!

Following your bug reports and feedback we have implemented the following changes:

Display Settings Fixes
We have overhauled the system for managing display settings to address cases that were not fixed by the previous patch. The changes include:

 When you change the resolution, display or window mode and select Apply in the Settings menu, the game now saves your changes without re-applying them.
 When you make changes in the Settings menu and select Revert, the game applies your previously saved display settings and refreshes the settings text once the changes have finished applying.
 When you select Defaults from the Settings menu, the game returns to your main display (the first one in the Display list) and uses that display's native resolution in Borderless window mode. If the native resolution is reported as portrait, the game translates it to landscape.

Known Issues and Limitations

 The UI is designed for a minimum aspect ratio of 16:10 (commonly used on laptops and handhelds), so we don't recommend using any narrower resolutions. The 4:3 and 5:4 resolutions are automatically filtered out.
 Portrait displays such as vertical monitors are not supported, so the game may behave unexpectedly if you try to move the game window to them.
 When setting the Window Mode to Fullscreen and using a resolution other than the display's native resolution, the game may not display correctly. If you need to use a non-native resolution, we recommend using Borderless window mode.
 You may see unusual resolutions in the list which are larger than your display's native resolution (e.g. some 1440p monitors may also list 4K as an option). This is normal as the game reads from the same list of resolutions available in Windows Display Settings, even if they cannot be applied.

Please Note
If the game launches in an incorrect resolution or does not let you select a playable resolution after installing this patch, please follow these troubleshooting guidelines:

Reset Settings to Defaults
The game may be trying to load an invalid resolution that was saved in a previous patch, so please try reverting your settings to defaults. If you cannot do this in-game, follow these steps:
[olist]
 Close the game.
 Delete your Settings.ini file which can be found in this folder: %USERNAME%/AppData/LocalLow/MilkyTea/Grit and Valor
 Launch the game again.
[/olist]
Report a Bug
If you have tried the above and the game still does not display correctly, please follow these steps to send us more information so we can debug the issue:
[olist]
 In your Steam Library, right-click the game and select Properties, then go to the Betas tab and enter the password fixthescreens. 
 Opt into the mt_debug_display branch which should appear.
 Download and install the beta update.
 Launch the game.
 Open the Display Debugger menu from the top of the screen. This menu is centered horizontally so it should be accessible even if the game launches in a narrow resolution.
 Take a screenshot of the game while the Display Debugger menu is open (press F12 to capture via Steam).
 Upload your screenshot and send it to us either in this Steam discussion or in the bug-reports channel on the Grit and Valor Discord.
[/olist]
Other Fixes

 Fixed Bomber Plane not appearing in the Advanced Combat levels in New Germany.
 Fixed dead units causing navigation issues and units to spin on the spot.
 Fixed tile issues in Western Europe levels in which inaccessible tiles were selectable, causing mech pathing issues.

Thanks for your patience while we have dealt with these bug reports. We appreciate all the feedback and will continue investigating any future reports. You can share your experiences here on Steam or via the official Discord.

The Grit and Valor - 1949 Team

notes.title: Mech Analysis: Leadslug
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders! 

Today we’re examining the Leadslug, a Ballistic-Class Mech manufactured by Sebika Ballistics. Its devastating shotguns unleash a ferocious spread of piercing rounds, causing destruction to anything in its path. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/a8b7eb1f5aec721c51564858dfe8d44f1cd6e975.jpg

BASE STATS 

 Health: 500 
 Armor: 0  
 Repair: 0  
 Movement Speed: 15 
 Damage: 15 
 Weapon Range: 2 
 Fire Rate: 120 
 Weakness Damage: 50% 
 High Ground Damage: 20%  
 Critical Chance: 0%  
 Critical Damage: 100% 

The Leadslug has consistent stats across the board with respectable movement speed, health, and standard critical/weakness damage output. Its key drawback is it’s below-average weapon-range of two tiles, meaning this mech needs to get up close and personal to confront enemies.  

It makes up for this with a high fire rate, ensuring that once you engage, you’ll be spraying Axis units with hail of bullets from its dual shotguns and extinguishing them quickly. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/1f1cb24d787f554a35b155e16b95e1174336a740.jpg

ABILITY PAIRINGS 
As a solid all-round unit, the Leadslug has flexible options for ability pairings. However we do have some preferences within the three provided by your starting pilots: 


 Archie Miller - Mech Jet: this is a prime choice since the Leadslug only has a weapon range of two tiles. Being able to jump in to engage your enemies quickly helps overcome any vulnerability from being exposed to Axis units with longer range for too long. 

 Emilia Rochefort - Mechano-Arm: another way to circumvent the Leadslug’s requirement to get close to enemies is with the Mechano-Arm to help it tank incoming damage. This is a great choice which enables the mech to play a bruiser-style role on the squad and relieve pressure from your other units. 

 Jan Novak - Deploy Mines: these are our third choice from the starting lineup. With a respectable movement speed, the Leadslug can get around the map well enough to drop mines in prime locations. However, these do less than the other two abilities to make up for the mech’s key weakness. 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/0b002ed627d6f8df2cd02780405241f071e107e8.jpg

Overall, the Leadslug is an impressive staple of the squad and is sure to output plenty of damage. If you can keep it repaired or armoured-up throughout a run, it’s sure to pay you back by obliterating your foes. Stay tuned for more intel on the remaining mech models! 

Stay up to date on game news and more by joining us on Discord!

notes.title: Mech Analysis: Clusterstorm
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders! 

It’s time to meet Clusterstorm, another Explosive Class mech! This absolute unit fires repeated cluster bombs which raze sections of the battlefield, leaving enemy units nowhere to flee. Use it to thin out entire wave of incoming foes for your other mechs to pick off at their leisure. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/f47073575c4483d7fc09179b78a31cdab46afcdf.jpg
KEY STATISTICS 
The Clusterstorm boasts a reliable spread of stats. Dealing 20 base damage per rocket raises the ceiling of each volley it fires. Complimented by a weapon range of 3 tiles, makes this perfect for dealing damage across entire squads of enemies. 

With a base health stat of 500, the Clusterstorm can be vulnerable compared to tankier units. Make sure to either get in first with enough firepower to wipe out anything that attacks it quickly or use other mechs to bear the brunt of the damage. 

A high base movement speed of 20 leaves the Clusterstorm surprisingly agile with the ability to reposition and make up for it’s lower health rating. If you ever need split the squad, it can quickly move across the map to support your remaining units where needed. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/e5b043241f795ccd7543d91b5ae3f8d5fe02e22f.jpg
ABILITY PAIRINGS 
Paired with the right ability, the Clusterstorm can be made even more effective in combat. Here some considerations for using it with the three abilities provided by your starting pilots: 

Archie Miller - Mech Jet: Double down on the Clusterstorm’s high rate of movement by allowing it to travel even faster with this jump ability. Doing so means you can cover ground faster than any other unit, to defend or capture objectives, gather air-dropped enhancements, and quickly return to the fight. 

Jan Novak - Deploy Mines: Being able to move quickly by default also makes the mines an interesting option. Allow your slower mechs to hold down the fort while sending out the Clusterstorm to strategic positions to place mines. 

Emilia Rochefort - Mechano-arm: To make up for the Clusterstorms key weakness (low health), you can give it this self-healing ability to make a more well-rounded unit. Allowing this mech to sustain additional damage will give it enough time to deal damage and defeat most enemies. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/5111f57cabea4e3ff2307d7bb29d476c22ca7d39.jpg
The Clusterstorm is an asset to any squad with its wide range of applications and ability to pair well with any given pilot. It comes with some additional pressure to protect another unit beyond just the Command Vehicle, but if you take of it, the Clusterstorm will take care of you back with efficiency in clearing out enemies. The Warbringer can take considerable damage before going down, though it relies on your positioning and support to endure. Movement Speed is moderate, making it less nimble than faster mechs but still capable of staying in combat without being too slow.

notes.title: Update: Control Scheme Improvements
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders!

Thank you as ever for your determined efforts to liberate the British Isles! Your feedback and reviews throughout the demo have been incredibly helpful. Based on your suggestions, we’re making changes to the controls. These are now live in the demo and will also feature in the final release on 26 March.

NOTE: Existing players will need to reset controls to default for some of these changes to take effect.

General Improvements
Unit Cycling
Previously, Cycling Units would default to the same mech, making moving your whole squad tedious with this method. It looked something like:
[olist]
 Press Cycle Units which would select the first unit (e.g. Ironclad).
 Move Ironclad to a tile, at which point the Ironclad gets deselected.
 Press Cycle Units, which selects the Ironclad again.
 Press Cycle Units again for it to then Select the next unit (e.g. Draqan).
[/olist]
Now, the system will automatically move along to the next unit in order by default to help you cycle through them more quickly.

Keyboard + Mouse Changes
Left Click/Right Click
Units are now selected with the left mouse button and moves with the right mouse button by default. This is more in line with other RTT and RTS games. The units’ colliders have also increased in size, making them easier to select quickly. We hope this makes manoeuvring your squad more fluid!
Gamepad and touch controls remain in the one-button style for convenience on those control schemes.

Gamepad Changes
Unit Cycling
Cycling through units is now bound to the left/right bumpers by default (previously left/right on the d-pad). This allows you to cycle through units at the same time as controlling the camera more easily.

Freeze Time
Moving the unit cycling to bumpers has displaced the default for the freeze-time binding. This is now moved to X (Button West), the last remaining free face button.

Thanks once again for all your suggestions! We firmly believe these changes will greatly improve the experience of quickly manoeuvring your squad. Let us know what you think, here on Steam and in our official Discord.

REMINDER: Existing players will need to reset controls to default for some of these changes to take effect.

The Grit and Valor – 1949 Team

notes.title: Mech Analysis: The Thunderhead
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders! 

Today’s briefing contains an analysis of the Thunderhead. This Explosive Class mech is the embodiment of heavy artillery dominance. Manufactured by Warhead, it comes equipped with a pair of powerful mortar cannons, each launching devastating high-explosive shells at its targets. With its overwhelming firepower, the Thunderhead is perfect for raining destruction from a distance, making it an invaluable asset for squads that favour long-range bombardment. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/7857a72b78a40921de22cda50692fc76d53810b7.jpg
KEY STATISTICS 
The Thunderhead is the powerhouse of [strike]the cell[/strike] long-range destruction. As an Explosive Class mech, it relies on its dual mortar cannons to deliver high-damage blasts.  

However, with a low Fire Rate and slow Movement Speed, the Thunderhead isn’t built for rapid engagements or quick repositioning. Instead, it thrives when you hold key positions, raining down fire from a distance thanks to its extended Weapon Range. Commanders should prioritize positioning, ensuring the Thunderhead remains protected while it shells enemy forces from afar. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/942f1335e41fd49b07755fdb1a1d9a2bdc613208.gif

ABILITY PAIRINGS 
The Thunderhead is a devastating long-range mech, but its slow Movement Speed and low Fire Rate mean it requires careful positioning and support to maximize its effectiveness. These ability pairings will help it stay in the fight and deliver its full explosive potential: 

 Archie Miller – Mech Jet: While the Thunderhead is built for long-range engagements, its low mobility makes it vulnerable when caught in close combat. Mech Jet allows you to reposition it quickly, either to gain a better vantage point or escape dangerous situations. This ability is especially useful for securing high ground, where the Thunderhead’s High Ground Damage bonus can deal even more destruction. 
 Jan Novak – Deploy Mines: Given its slow Fire Rate, the Thunderhead can struggle against fast-moving enemies who close the distance before it can fire. Deploy Mines provides an extra layer of defense, creating deadly zones that punish aggressive enemies before they reach firing range. Combined with its explosive mortar blasts, this pairing turns the battlefield into a minefield of destruction. 
 Emilia Rochefort – Mechano-arm: The Thunderhead is at risk of being overrun if enemies manage to push past its bombardment. The Mechano-arm offers health regeneration, allowing it to stay in battle longer and maintain sustained fire from the backlines.  
These ability pairings allow the Thunderhead to overcome its weaknesses and remain a dominant force in long-range warfare. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/3fa10862c63aa6bdae4f3d609a1b031fd09689a3.gif

We hope this analysis helps you make the most of the Thunderhead! With the right positioning and support, it can annihilate enemies from a distance, providing your squad with unmatched firepower. Stay tuned for further reports on the remaining mech models.

notes.title: Mech Analysis: The Draqan
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders!

This report brings intel regarding the Draqan, a Fire Class mech. Manufactured by Forge Industries, this fearsome machine is built for destruction. Its flamethrowers engulf all enemy forces caught in their path, leaving nothing but scorched wreckage in its wake. While specializing in fiery devastation, it remains a well-rounded choice for commanders that require aggressive frontline power.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/d04ebbf526ddc65fa233c706138e821c40da7e29.jpg
KEY STATISTICS 
The Draqan is a relentless force on the battlefield, bringing the full destructive power of the Fire Class to bear. Equipped with devastating flamethrowers, this mech specializes in close-quarters combat, incinerating anything in its path with a high Fire Rate and consistent Damage output. 

With its high Mobility, you can swiftly reposition the Draqan to control key areas, secure Enhancements drops, and apply relentless pressure to enemy forces. Its short Weapon Range requires smart positioning, but in the right hands, this mech is a nightmare for any opponent caught within its fiery reach! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/a0dd648cd84c24ba9d45d60d0a6c31d07dff6aac.gif

ABILITY PAIRINGS 
Consider these combinations for maximum effectiveness: 

 Archie Miller – Mech Jet: With moderate Health, the Draqan relies on mobility to stay alive. The Mech Jet allows it to leap across the battlefield, helping it close the gap on enemies or reposition quickly when overwhelmed. The landing impact deals damage, making it an excellent opener before unleashing its high-speed flamethrower attacks. 
 Jan Novak – Deploy Mines: Since the Draqan excels in close-quarters combat but lacks defensive durability, Deploy Mines reinforces your zone control. Enemies forced to move through chokepoints will take heavy mine damage before reaching the Draqan, making it easier to capitalize on its high Weakness Damage bonus and incinerate opponents as they stagger through its fiery range. 
 Emilia Rochefort – Mechano-arm: With moderate Health and no built-in Repair or Armor, the Draqan can’t afford prolonged fights without support. The Mechano-arm provides health regeneration, ensuring it can remain on the frontlines longer. This is especially useful as the Draqan can continue melting enemies without retreating too often. 


These ability pairings help the Draqan become an unstoppable force in battle, turning its short-range but relentless firepower into a game-changing advantage. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/180f00dae89ed24d43667d5a8906e137d3c35d43.gif

We trust this intel will aid your assessment of the Draqan! When deployed effectively, this firestorm of a mech can dominate the battlefield, forcing enemies to retreat or be reduced to ashes. Stay tuned for further reports on the remaining mechs.

notes.title: Grit and Valor – 1949 | End of Year Roundup
notes.content:
Commanders, it’s been a glorious year for the Resistance.  

To cap off our 2024, we’re rounding up some of our Grit and Valor highlights and briefly hinting at what’s to come in 2025. 

Unveiling Grit and Valor – 1949

May 30th 2024, was the day we revealed Grit and Valor to the world. To cast your mind back, here’s a look at that very first reveal trailer.  
 
[previewyoutube=QReoFOX8Y2k;full][/previewyoutube]
 
In our press release we described the game as “A dieselpunk real-time tactics roguelite...set in an alternate reality Europe where World War 2 rages on and the Evil Axis controls the continent. As the last hope to end this brutal conflict, players must join the resistance and escort an EMP device into the heart of enemy territory and destroy their mech production and communications headquarters – Machine Tower.”  
 
We were massively grateful for the positive reaction this initial announcement received – it spurred us on to get something playable into your hands... 

Our First Public Demo

July was a big one for us. Just over a month after our announcement, we released our first public demo. We were eager to bring you along with us for the journey, and allow you to provide direct feedback to help shape the future of our game. 
 
[previewyoutube=ZxVolxS9pGg;full][/previewyoutube] 
 
It was also significant for us to see swathes of great influencers and content creators getting to grips with their mech squads. Our teams were thrilled to see people they were already big fans of - such as Barbarous King and Splattercatgaming - experiencing something they’d had a hand in creating!  
 
Taking Grit on the Road

We’ve also been lucky enough to bring Grit to players, press, and industry heads at a bunch of events throughout the year.
 
In June, shortly after its announcement, Grit and Valor had a presence on the show floor at Guerilla Collective’s ‘The Mix’ event in LA.  
 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/b42f635d864ec1b1f9188e652e8c240d20b2632a.jpg
 
Later, in August, the Grit Team were in Seattle during PAX West to showcase Grit once more at a great Guerilla Collective event.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/2bcceea026e57bfe7afe01381389b32fcdee0dbd.jpg
 
Then in late September, Grit had something of a homecoming when we brought it to FORMAT Liverpool – held a stone’s throw from the studio in which it’s being developed.  
 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/44ae0a26ca6f33ea79dea40ad9f0dd267127123f.jpg

We’re eagerly anticipating further events appearances in 2025.

notes.title: Upcoming Features Deep Dive #1 – Run Rewards!
notes.content:
Attention, Commanders! 
 
We've received fresh intel on upcoming changes to Grit and Valor’s Run Rewards systems. 
 
As mentioned previously, your feedback on the demo has been helping our teams massively in finding new ways to make Grit’s tactical gameplay sing.  

Now that the Closed Beta is live, we’re going to be delving in to a wealth of additional feedback. Here’s an overview of some changes to rewards that are already in the works! 

WHAT ARE RUN REWARDS?

If you’re a Roguelite/Roguelike veteran – feel free to skip ahead! 
 
If you’re new to Roguelites, a ‘Run’ is what you begin each time you’re defeated on the battlefield. 
 
Run Rewards, then, represent the progression you make over the course of a run. 
 
To make matters more complex – in Roguelites this progression can be split in two; Standard Progression and Meta Progression. 

 {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/13f90d87f47e56edce23befc3c61488ba353f22f.png
 
In the case of Grit and Valor – 1949, ‘Standard Progression’ represents the temporary enhancements you get during a run. 
 
‘Meta Progression’ represents the permanent upgrades you’re able to make back at the Resistance Base and carry with you in future runs. 
 
RUN REWARD IMPROVEMENTS: STANDARD PROGRESSION

Reward Frequency

We noticed that only offering mid-run upgrades at the end of a mission meant long breaks between upgrading your squad over the course of a run!  
 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/0f61ba1d9562b87a692a5f00e42185380e7cf7d1.gif
 
In future you’ll notice rewards "dropping" during a mission. You’ll need to assess on the fly whether to bring your Mechs out of cover to go procure them, adding an entirely new risk-vs-reward dynamic to your moment-to-moment gameplay. 

Improved Enhancements 

To make choosing enhancements and going for a specific build more meaningful, we’re going to improve their effects and even create synergies between different Enhancement types. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/d3b7279019d802ef217af8937def03005ba7a972.gif

RUN REWARD IMPROVEMENTS: META PROGRESSION
 

New Pilots!

We’ll also be introducing some new Pilots – each with unique never-before-seen abilities! We can’t wait to tell you more about them in a later blog...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/9957fad903ee627454811c1466d9c19c867c9f8c.png
 

Pilot Ability Augmentations 

We’re also exploring new ways to give you more control over how you set up your squad. In the future, Grit and Valor will allow you to augment existing Pilot Abilities to make them behave exactly the way you like. 
 
Take the Mech Jet Ability, for instance. With Pilot Ability Augmentations, a cautious player could augment this ability mid-run to be able to jump then immediately jump back to its starting position. Alternatively, an offensively minded Commander could augment that same ability to drop mines as it jumps. 
 
We took your feedback and some inspiration from other satisfying Roguelite systems for this! It should give you even more variety on each run! 
 
--- 

We hope this has given you some valuable insight into how we’re using your feedback to improve the game’s rewards system ahead of launch. In the coming weeks, we’ll be sharing more of these deep dives on other aspects of Grit and Valor Gameplay! 

If you’d like to help with future changes, apply to our Ambassador program where we hold regular playtests. You can also join our Discord for extra behind-the-scenes content! 
 
The Grit and Valor – 1949 Team

notes.title: Upcoming Features!
notes.content:
Since releasing the demo for Grit & Valor, we’ve learned a ton about what makes roguelite and tactical games feel rewarding—and we can’t wait to bring that experience to life. We’ve gone through every comment, crunched the game data, and we can’t wait to show you what’s coming next. Here’s an overview of what’s in the works!

Run Rewards 
Get ready for major improvements to the rewards you’ll score both mid-run and back at base! We’re dialling up the impact of your choices, adding more variety, and making every decision feel bigger and bolder.
 
[olist]
 Reward Frequency + Mid-Run Rewards: we noticed that only offering mid-run upgrades at the end of a mission meant long breaks between upgrading your squad over the course of a run. We’re looking at "dropping" upgrades during a mission, causing players to choose whether they can risk collection. 
 Playstyle-Altering Rewards: taking inspiration from upgrades like the Daedalus Hammer in Hades, you will be able to augment Pilot Abilities, fundamentally changing the way they behave. We expect this to greatly increase the uniqueness of every run. 
 Improved Enhancements: to make choosing enhancements and going for a specific build more meaningful, we’re going to improve their effects and create synergies between different Enhancement types.
[/olist]
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/ae55b69fb0533d31d7b446eca3eebb9b8134654c.jpg
More Pilots and Abilities
Our demo contained four Pilots, each with a unique ability. To increase varirety, we’re examining options such as allowing duplicate pilot abilities within a squad as well as adding more abilities. Each option would offer both more content to unlock throughout the game and greater variety! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/9957fad903ee627454811c1466d9c19c867c9f8c.png
The Opening Gameplay Experience 
In the demo, players went from controlling one Mech in a safe environment during the tutorial to controlling three plus the Command Vehicle in a live mission. To help familiarise first-time players with the mechanics, unlocking Mechs and Pilots will be made more gradual. 
 
Similarly, Pilot Abilities appeared to add a layer of complexity too early on and were underused in early levels. Gradual unlocking and UI improvements to better communicate when abilities can be used will make this easier.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/a6dafabff3d858b1a53e05094cb9e0b3012e81e0.png
Combining the Mechyard and Scrapyard 
Moving between the Mechyard and Scrapyard to buy modules and then upgrade mechs was more cumbersome than we would like. Combining these spaces should streamline the upgrading experience by requiring fewer steps.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/cfc6fd2e41ed86db67e69d4c2d603c8323b8304e.png
Casual Mode 
To offer a fun experience to our more casual audience, we’re working on a more forgiving difficulty. This will likely be stat-based and allows us to maintain the current level of challenge for players who prefer it.

The Command Centre 
The Command Vehicle will receive its own progression system, via the Command Centre, a new location within the hub. Here, you will be able to unlock and upgrade further abilities for the Command Vehicle, making it more integral and useful part of the squad in battle. 

The Command Centre will also allow players to unlock other mechanics and progression systems within the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/c18e8f37471b5a5a21e0ceca2a9fa0c43fb34841.png
Region Map Changes 
[olist]
 Random Narrative Nodes: having the option to choose a narrative node missed an opportunity for spontaneous moments. We’re addressing this by introducing more choice, strategy and variability into the Region Map. Our exploration here is designed to make these events feel more natural when they arise.
 Reviving Mechs: losing a mech during a run can be devastating, especially if your build focused on enhancing that specific type. Shop nodes and starting currency will be adjusted to make it easier to buy back a mech, especially if one is lost early in the run.
[/olist]

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/cd58e296ed0a184867fcfd28951e365bd5849986.png
Highlighting Time Controls
Many players in the demo found and enjoyed the time controls allowing the game to be slowed down or even paused while they assessed and issued commands. However, due to time constraints, these were only previously available via the Settings menu and unbound by default. These controls will be added to the UI along with other general UI improvements.

notes.title: Grit and Valor – 1949 | Progression & Upgrades Explained
notes.content:
Attention Commanders!

In Grit and Valor – 1949, each run pits your mech squad against overwhelming odds. 

To liberate Europe from the evil Axis Forces, you’re going to need to make the most of every upgrade and enhancement you can get your hands on.   

So buckle in!  

Here's a 101 on the ins and outs of the progression system, and how your decisions can be the difference between disastrous defeats and valiant victories.   
 
How Progression and Rewards Work  

For fans of the Roguelite genre aspects of this may be familiar, but let's get into the specifics. 
 
In Grit and Valor – 1949, there are three core aspects to the progression system: 

[olist]
Mid-Run Progression:  

During each campaign you’ll have the opportunity to boost your mechs with a choice of temporary end of level enhancements. You’ll also get the chance to buy temporary shop boosts and get narrative event rewards.
End-of-Run Rewards:  

When your run ends, you’ll bank a range of meta currencies to spend back at the Resistance Base. Occasionally, you’ll unlock new pilots, too.
Between-Run Progression: 

At the Resistance Base, you’ll spend your earned currency on mech modules that you can equip to permanently upgrade your mechs. It’s here that you’ll able to purchase new mechs, and level up your pilot abilities.
[/olist]

Now, let's explore these in more detail...  

Mid-Run Progression 

In Grit and Valor – 1949, mid-run progression is all about building up temporary enhancements to increase your chances of success, while banking Black Coins to spend along the way. 

Enhancements

Enhancements are temporary stat upgrades for your mechs that last until your run ends. At the end of each successful mission, you’ll be presented with a choice of three.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/1ad22d950948e4e1b8b53878280fe5d23ca22ac9.png

Enhancements range from Common to Legendary and can offer big boosts to a variety of mech stats including damage, damage resistance, fire rate, critical damage and much more.  
 
Remember to choose wisely. Picking enhancements that suit your mech squad and your playstyle is essential. If you’re dissatisfied with your roll, spend some Black Coins to reroll. 

It’s important to note that opting to take on Advanced Combat and Elite Combat missions will give you a greater chance of picking up rare enhancement. These missions are far more deadly, however, so we’ll leave it to you to weigh up the risk vs reward. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/a7406cc8cafc56ca3b3a73722e9950f574354786.jpg

Scenarios 

Between levels, you’ll occasionally be given the choice to avoid combat altogether and instead progress by choosing a ‘Scenario’ - a narrative dilemma that requires your Commander instincts. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/4ddeee095878d372f18f9f74b4ca240563e04c47.jpg

Scenarios will vary in content – and we wouldn’t want to spoil any narrative bits - but in this example, you find a broken Axis mech and can choose between salvaging it for a random enhancement and using its part to repair your mechs or give them a health boost for the remainder of your run. 

The Scavenger’s Shop

Another mid-run opportunity for you to enhance your squad is the Scavenger.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/780e9a0ee35a14eb00cb8615c5ca4c621e673898.jpg

Like Scenarios, you’ll encounter the Scavenger on the campaign map between missions and be given the option trade your Black Coins for enhancements or Scrap. These run-ins with the Scavenger are rare, but could save your squad in a pinch. 

End-of-Run Rewards 

End-of-Run Rewards come in the form of Scrap, Valor, and Blueprints.  

These are the essential resources you’ll need to use to acquire lasting upgrades back at the Resistance Base, such as new Mechs, enhanced Pilot abilities, and Upgrade Modules for your existing Mechs. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/8f4be99f6bce0518fee9493eeb48916072ee8977.jpg

The amount of Scrap, Valor, and Blueprints you gain will depend on your run's success. 

Tackling those Advanced and Elite missions, achieving your bonus goals, and eliminating more Axis forces will increase the amount you receive at the end of a run. 

Here’s a little more on what each currency is used for: 


 Scrap - A currency used to purchase Upgrade Modules from the Junkyard Shop at the Resistance Base.
Valor - Valor is applied to individual Pilots at the Pilot Barracks to increase their skills.  
Blueprints - Blueprints can be used to either unlock new mechs or buy traits for them at the Mech Yard.
 

Between Run Progression 

Here’s where you can make a lasting impact. Upgrades you make to your Mech Squad back at Resistance Base are permanent. Let’s dive into what you can do.  

Buy Mech Modules at the Junkyard Shop

Spend your scrap wisely at the Junkyard Shop on Upgrade Modules for your Mechs. Like Enhancements, Modules range from Common to Legendary.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/3538a720dde5b113c9e7aa0ec9d613ff94b58e2d.jpg

Apply Modules and Traits at the Mech Yard 

Once you’ve purchased some Upgrade Modules, head to the Mech Yard to have Reggie Steele apply them to your mechs. 

Optimise your squad however you see fit. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/69544f81488f1ed6ff2384f14a8aa869217ee4ef.jpg

In this example, the Commander has wisely addressed one of the Thunderhead’s weaknesses, movement speed, by equipping a +30% Module. 

Unlock New Mechs 

At the Mech Yard – if you have acquired enough blueprints, you can use them to requisition the development of powerful new mechs. 

Upgrade Pilot Abilities 

Next stop, the Pilot Barracks. 

Providing your Pilots with the Valor they need to succeed is part of every capable Commander’s pre-run ritual. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/305d9d395c4b089fb8e60df7ec2560d9f147e5b3.jpg

Here, Emilia Rochefort’s Mechano-arm ability has been boosted. In combat, you’ll now be able to use the ability more often and it’ll repair more damage. 

---
 
Congratulations, Commander. You’ve passed your Progression & Upgrades 101 with flying colours.  

Now what’re you waiting for? Go and apply what you’ve learned in the field. 

Let ‘em have it!

notes.title: Grit and Valor – 1949 | Play the Demo!
notes.content:
Greetings Commander!  
 
We’re delighted to announce that Grit and Valor – 1949: is now available to play in our Steam demo! In preparation, we’re sharing this brief on your ultimate objective of freeing Europe mission by mission, region by region. 

Your goal as Commander of the Resistance is to deliver the EMP weapon and disable the Axis Machine Tower in the heart of New Germany. To get there, you will traverse four regions, freeing them from the enemy’s occupying forces along the way. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/4cfeee635e9f9be2e06c02db0313e453d85b02be.jpg
To progress through a region, you must dive into a series of missions and defeat waves of enemies. This is achieved by moving your squad of three mechs and the all-important Command Vehicle and responding to the evolving battlefield in real-time. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/237a813ac943c83354f89475740a0314e3f74ccf.png
Choosing the right position for your mechs is critical. Here are some tactics to bear in mind:  


 Place your mechs between enemies and your Command Vehicle to protect it 
 Use elevated tiles to gain a Critical Damage bonus against enemy units 
 Engage enemy units with mechs that have a damage type-advantage 
 Shield your mechs using cover 

When you have mastered these tactics, you may also complete Bonus Objectives if you are daring enough! These include capturing radio towers and defending important buildings. Doing so rewards you with Black Coins which can be spent on upgrades in the Scavenger’s shop during your run.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/75348069bd2cdf3ac9df013d81b3a2e7aa1491ef.jpg
As you complete missions, you will carve your path through the region. Along the way, you can choose which missions to take to maximise your chances of success. Here are some factors which might influence the direction you take:  

Enhancements: choose temporary upgrades to work best with your squad build. Some missions offer a greater chance of rare Enhancement rewards. 

Black Coins: Bonus Objectives reward the Black Coin currency (in-run upgrades). 

Scavenger Supplies: An encounter with the Scavenger offers the chance to spend your Black Coins on replenishing squad Health, Mech Armor, Enhancements and more. 

Hazards and Elites: Missions featuring Hazards such as enemy Bomber Planes or Elite enemy mechs offer an increased chance of rare Enhancement rewards. 

Region Events: Chance encounters along the journey offers the player a difficult choice, and possible rewards and dangers. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/f68c009f5c5758afb9ce4b0ba231288393d820fb.jpg
When your run is over, you will also be rewarded with Scrap, Valor, and Blueprints. These currencies allow you to purchase permanent upgrades in the Resistance Base such as new Mechs, improved Pilots skills, and Upgrade Modules for your existing Mechs. 

The amount of Scrap, Valor, and Blueprints you’re rewarded with will scale depending on your performance in the run, by completing more missions, bonus objectives and taking down more of the Axis forces your rewards will increase. 

We trust this overview will help when the time comes to free regions from the grip of the Axis Powers. Should you fail, you can return to base to make necessary upgrades and redeploy. We will share more intel on how to build the ultimate mech squad in a future transmission. 

To stay up to date on news and announcements join our Discord server and sign up to our newsletter! 

The Grit and Valor – 1949 Team

notes.title: Grit and Valor - 1949 | FAQS
notes.content:
GENERAL INFORMATION

WHAT IS GRIT AND VALOR - 1949?
Grit and Valor is a real-time tactics roguelite set in an alternate-history WWII dieselpunk setting. To complete a run, players complete grid-based levels defeating waves of enemies by tactically manoeuvring their units. Between runs, you can spend earned resources to upgrade your squad to help reach further levels and regions.

WHO ARE THE DEVELOPERS?
The game is developed by Milky Tea, an indie studio based in Liverpool, UK.

WHICH PLATFORMS IS THE GAME ON?
The game is available on Steam and set to release on PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch, Xbox Series X and Series S simultaneously next year.

WHAT ARE THE PC SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS?
Minimum:

 OS: Windows 10 64-bit
 Processor: 2.4 GHz Quad Core
 Memory: 8 GB RAM
 Graphics: Nvidia GTX 960 / Radeon R9 280
 DirectX: Version 11
 Storage: 5 GB available space

Recommended:

 OS: Windows 10/11 64-bit
 Processor: 2.5+ GHz Quad Core
 Memory: 16 GB RAM
 Graphics: Nvidia GTX 2060 / Radeon RX 5600 XT
 DirectX: Version 11
 Storage: 5 GB available space

WHERE CAN I PLAY?
Our free demo is going live on July 24th, 2024 on Steam!

WHICH LANGUAGES ARE AVAILABLE?
At launch, the game will be available in: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian, Ukranian, Brazilian-Portuguese, Korean, Japanese, Traditional Chinese & Simplified Chinese.

GAMEPLAY

WHAT IS THE OBJECTIVE?
Your goal is to make your way through four regions, one at a time by completing their levels and final boss. In the demo, you are tasked with liberating the first region: the British Isles.

HOW DO I NAVIGATE THE GAME'S INTERFACE AND MENUS?
Mouse controls (point and click) can be used to navigate the UI or controller buttons to select and command your units.

WHAT ARE THE BASIC CONTROLS?
To move your units, select them and then select the tile you wish to move them to. Combat is automatic, based on your unit's attack range which is shown when the unit is selected.

ARE THERE DIFFICULTY SETTINGS?
The difficulty is at a fixed level, designed to be challenging. Being a roguelite, early levels should become easier over time as your tactics and squad improve.

HOW DO I MANAGE PILOT ABILITIES?
Pilot abilities can be upgraded in the Pilot's Barracks at your base using Valor, which is earned at the end of each run.

HOW DO I UPGRADE MY MECHS?
Mechs can be upgraded with modules bought from the Junkyard and applied at the Mech Yard at your base.

WHAT TYPES OF MISSIONS ARE THERE?
Each mission has the goal of surviving all enemy waves with random Bonus Objectives offering variety (e.g. point capture, delivery and more).

CAN I REPLAY MISSIONS?
Regions can be replayed at any time when selecting your campaign from resistance base between runs.

TECHNICAL HELP

HOW DO I REPORT BUGS OR LEAVE FEEDBACK?
We continually check the discussion area on Steam as well as our Discord server. If you need support, the Discord server has a ticket system for us to help you directly.

HOW DO I ADJUST GRAPHICAL/DISPLAY SETTINGS?
Settings such as resolution and display modes can be accessed using the Esc key and navigating to Settings > Graphics.

COMMUNITY

IS THERE AN OFFICIAL DISCORD SERVER?
Yes! You can find our OFFICIAL DISCORD SERVER here.

HOW DO I CONTACT SUPPORT?
For any issues you experience during the demo we recommend using the ticketing system within our Discord server.

WHERE I CAN I FOLLOW THE GAME ON SOCIAL MEDIA?
We are on all the main channels (X, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok) which can be found by search Grit and Valor - 1949. Links are also available within the Discord.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/e1a071b1f231649e8e3ea00f4c78bd3be6cbd17e.png

As you embark on your journey through Grit & Valor - 1949, here's your strategic guide to success:

1. Enter Unlocked Region: Starting in the British Isles, you must fight your way through Europe to New Germany.

2. Choose a Level: Each level has unique risks and rewards. Choose the optimal path into the heart of the enemy to maximise your chance of success.

3. Assess the Terrain & Mission Type: Consider where enemies may appear, areas to use as cover, and additional bonus objectives to complete.

4. Protect the Command Vehicle and Survive Enemy Waves: Your primary objective is to protect the Command Vehicle, but you can complete bonus objectives to earn additional rewards.

5. Return to Your Resistance Base: After success or failure in the last region, you will return to your Resistance Base, allowing access to your team of engineers.

6. Upgrade Your Pilots, Mechs, and Command Vehicle: Use the resources gained from battling the Axis forces to upgrade your Squad.

Prepare meticulously, Commanders. Your decisions will shape the course of history!

Join the conversation on Discord to hear more about the core gameplay loop and additional features!
